text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi called for all the people to help oversee the affairs of the state and government and to fight against corruption, smuggling, wastefulness, vindictiveness toward subordinates and abuse of vested power to suppress people.
-- The Ministry of Trade reported a trade deficit of $1.14 billion in the first five months of this year, equivalent to 60.5 percent of the deficit in the same period of 1997.
-- The army's political department delegation concluded an eight-day visit to China which was aimed at strengthening friendship and solidarity between the armies and peoples of the two countries.
-- Industrial Parks' (IP) authorities will begin to issue, revise and retract licences for foreign investment projects at IP and export processing zones as of July 1.
-- A delegation of European Union experts arrived in Vietnam to prepare for negotiations and renewal of the textiles trade agreement between Vietnam and the union.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam has implemented a project to set up a deposit insurance company to protect small, individual depositors.
-- The Communist Party's Central Committee has called upon the entire Party, people and army to exercise their mastery and take an active part in building the state.
-- A woman was sentenced to death and four other people were sent to jail by the Quang Ninh province court for selling 1.8 kg of heroin.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong said tobacco production will be a state monopoly and that a special, very high consumption tax will be applied to the sale of tobacco.
-- Vietnam sold 100 bilion dong ($8.57 million) worth of one-year Treasury notes with an annual coupon of 11.95 percent to five domestic institutions on Wednesday.
